payload.headline: Micron jumps 11.89% on no reported news; priced for boom margins to last

summary.thesis: Micron is an A-grade business earning record margins, and the 811.3 price already assumes most of today's cash flow holds, leaving little cushion if margins fade.
summary.decision: Hold. Wait for a pullback toward support before adding, and make no swing trade until the price clears resistance or tests support.

payload.happening: MU closed at 811.3 on 2026-11-11, up 11.89% on the day. Our data shows no news since the last note. By 10:54 ET it was trading at 785.4, which is intraday and not a close. The next earnings report is due 2026-12-23.
payload.business: Nothing in today's data changes the business itself. The jump looks like a shift in sentiment, not new facts about demand, margins or cash. The business is very strong right now. Trailing revenue was 133.2B, up from 37.4B. Quarterly sales grew 345.03% year over year, faster than the 196.29% two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations as a share of sales) is 74.59%, up from 26.14%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose from 1.7B to 59.0B. The balance sheet is not at risk: 40.6B net cash and only 2.8B of debt. Dilution is modest at 1.78% a year. What is at risk is how long these margins last. The filings flag the 75% operating margin as the top of a 5-year range that runs from -41% to 75%, and memory chip prices have historically moved in boom-and-bust cycles (general knowledge). Insiders sold $14.0M outside pre-set plans. That is a governance and sentiment note, not a business change. We have no segment data to show which products are driving the growth.

worth.text: On today's earnings MU looks cheap: 10.9 times trailing earnings, and 6.9 times sales against a peer median of 8.6. But those earnings come from a peak year. The model gives no full discounted-cash-flow value, because a one-year jump from 1.7B to 59.0B in free cash flow can't be projected forward. The price implies starting free-cash-flow growth of only 2.8%. In other words, the market is paying roughly for today's cash flow to hold, not to keep rising. If cash flow simply stays flat, the value is 724.81. If it grows 10% a year, the value is 1073.53. If the operating margin falls to 37%, even with 20% starting growth, the value is 805.56, about today's price. Against its own history, price-to-sales sits at the 78th percentile of its 5-year range. That history implies 322.32 to 833.11 per share, with a midpoint of 490.66. The gap between methods comes from one question: are today's margins the new normal or a cyclical peak? My range is 724.81 to 833.11, which puts the price near the top of it.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow stays near today's 59.0B rather than falling back as the 74.59% operating margin fades.

bull: Growth is speeding up, not slowing: quarterly revenue rose 345.03% year over year, against 196.29% two quarters ago, and grew 30.81% from the prior quarter.
Against peers it is cheap: price-to-sales of 6.9 versus a peer median of 8.6, and a growth-adjusted EV/sales ratio (company value to sales, adjusted for growth) of 0.32 times its peers.
If cash flow keeps growing even 10% a year, the model value is 1073.53. Meanwhile, 40.6B of net cash protects the downside.
bear: The operating margin of 74.59% (up from 26.14%) sits at the top of its 5-year range, and the filings note that peaks like this usually fade.
If the operating margin falls to 37%, the model value is 805.56, below today's 811.3. That leaves no margin of safety.
Against its own history the stock is expensive: price-to-sales is at the 78th percentile of its 5-year range, and the midpoint of that range implies only 490.66.

levels.what: Top of the 730.16–745.36 support zone. It sits close to the 724.81 value that assumes flat cash flow, so it is a better place to add.
Top of the own-history valuation range. Above it, the price assumes more than holding today's peak, so it is a level to reconsider and possibly trim.
Lower support zone (643.4–658.6, two touches). A break below it would signal the market doubts the margins.

longterm.why: The business is A-grade and cash-rich, but at 811.3 the price already assumes peak cash flow roughly holds. Holding makes sense, while adding is better done closer to 745.36.

swing.why: The price is in a sideways range. It sits below the falling 20-day average of 849.67 and the 50-day average of 950.43, and resistance at 846.03–861.22 is close overhead. With a daily ATR (average daily trading range) of 60.8, the reward to resistance is small for the risk. Better setups are a close above 861.22 or a test of the 730.16–745.36 support zone that holds.

decision.timing: Options price a 9.4% move by 2026-11-20 and 21.6% by 2027-01-15, which includes the 2026-12-23 earnings report. Large positions before that report carry event risk, and the report will show whether margins are holding.

change_mind: The 2026-12-23 report shows operating margin holding near 74.59% and quarter-over-quarter growth near 30.81%. That would support the 1073.53 growth case and move the view toward add.
A daily close above 861.22, the top of resistance, turns the swing view to enter. A close below 643.4 turns the long-term view more cautious.
Operating margin falling toward 37% means the value drops to about 805.56 or lower, which would support trimming above 833.11.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
